sy_guide.title: Ministry of Agriculture, Syria: guide to importing animals, animal products and by-products
sy_guide.lead_in: Under the Ministry of Agriculture’s July 2021 import guide:

uae.municipalities: The municipalities of each emirate oversee inspection at the port, testing, label approval and the release of imported shipments.
uae.aquatic: Farmed fish must not be fed pork protein. Wild-caught fish must be identified as wild-caught on a health certificate issued by the competent authority of the exporting country.
uae.labels: Under UAE.S GSO 9:2019, food labels must be in Arabic, and any other language used must match the Arabic text. This applies to bulk and retail packaging.
uae.dates: Production and expiry dates must appear directly on the original label or primary packaging; dates printed only on stickers are not accepted.
uae.zad: Under Ministerial Decree No. 239 of 2018, imported food must be registered in the national ZAD system before it is handled in UAE markets.

kuwait.resolution: Ministerial Resolution No. 6 of 2023 of the Public Authority for Food and Nutrition regulates imported food. It took effect on 1 September 2023 and cancelled the regulations issued under Resolution No. 19 of 2017.
kuwait.high_risk: The resolution classes fish as high-risk food, together with meat, poultry and dairy products.
kuwait.documents: Each food consignment must carry a customs declaration, a certificate of origin, a delivery permit, a trade licence or import permit, a health certificate and a packing list issued by the exporting facility.
kuwait.certificate_issuer: The health certificate must be issued and endorsed by the official regulatory authority of the country of origin or export.
kuwait.certificate_content: The health certificate must be in Arabic and/or English and state the number of packages, the total weight and the production batches.
kuwait.inspection: The Imported Food Department inspects consignments at the border port. Its inspectors may take samples for testing in the authority’s own or accredited laboratories.
kuwait.model_certificate: The authority publishes a bilingual model health certificate for fish exported to Kuwait, with fields for the temperature category (chilled, frozen or ambient), HS code, production date, expiry date and batch number.
kuwait.raqeb: In the authority’s Raqeb clearance guide, a fish import licence is a required attachment for fish, and a health certificate from the country of origin is required for all food.

bahrain.ports: The Ministry of Health inspects imported food at the three ports of entry: the sea port, air cargo and the causeway.
bahrain.importer: Food importers need a commercial registration from the Ministry of Industry and Commerce and a public health certificate to practise commercial activities under health surveillance.
bahrain.registration: Regular foods need no prior registration before import but must comply with Gulf (GSO) standards; prior registration applies to functional foods such as baby food.
bahrain.arrival: On arrival, the importer’s representative fills in the imported food inspection form and attaches the customs declaration, the packing list, the delivery order or bill of lading, and the health certificates.
bahrain.health_certificate: Every consignment needs an original health certificate from the competent authority of the country of origin, attesting compliance with GCC requirements, stamped and signed by the issuing authority.
bahrain.labels: Labels must be in Arabic; any other language must appear alongside the Arabic and match it.
bahrain.dates: Under GSO 150-1, chilled perishable foods containing fish carry mandatory expiry dates; for prepackaged food, stickers for production and expiry dates are not permitted.
bahrain.inspection: Inspection checks the container, the labels and sensory quality and, for chilled food, signs of defrosting and the container temperature records. When samples are taken for testing on a risk basis, the shipment is held until the results are known.

lebanon.registration: Ministry of Agriculture Decision 964 of 2011 requires every establishment that imports chilled or frozen fish to register with the Directorate of Animal Wealth, Department of Import and Export.
lebanon.labels: Decision 264/1 of 2013 requires the fish name on package labels to match its Arabic, English and scientific names and the names in all attached certificates; otherwise entry is refused.
lebanon.inspection: Decision 496/1 of 2010 makes imported fish and fish products subject to inspection and examination before entry into Lebanon is permitted.
lebanon.commitment: Decision 547/1 of 2012 lets fresh fish enter if the importer submits a commitment attested by a notary; a repeated violation within one year bars imports from the same source.
lebanon.cold_chain_record: Decision 573/1 of 2009 requires the cooling temperature of chilled and frozen food to be recorded throughout shipping.
lebanon.veterinary_certificate: Imported animal products must come with a veterinary health certificate issued by the authorities of the country of origin.
lebanon.origin_certificate: A certificate of origin must be authenticated by a chamber of commerce, industry or agriculture or another authenticating body.
lebanon.seal: The bill of lading must show Lebanon as the destination, and the container seal applied in the country of origin must be intact on arrival.

qatar.control: The ministry’s Port Health and Food Control Section controls imported food, fish included, under Food Control Law No. 8 of 1990 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2014.
qatar.health_certificate: Each consignment must carry a health certificate in Arabic, English or both; the guide includes a template for products of aquatic animal origin.
qatar.detention: A consignment may be held (temporary release) if its health certificate was issued before the food’s production date or after its shipment date.
qatar.inspection: Inspectors at the port check the vehicle, container and packs, check the labels and their language, and take samples from new items or according to the level of risk.
qatar.watheq: Food establishments must register in the ministry’s WATHEQ system; only registered companies can file import or export declarations through the Al Nadeeb system.
qatar.third_party: The ministry publishes a list of approved third-party bodies for pre-shipment inspection at origin; their certificates of conformity must be issued before export, not after.

iraq.cosqc: The Central Organization for Standardization and Quality Control (COSQC), an agency of the Ministry of Planning, enforces standards for imported products.
iraq.licence: Importers of food of animal origin request preliminary approval from the Ministry of Agriculture, and the Ministry of Trade then issues the import licence.
iraq.certificates: Food of animal origin needs a certificate of origin certified by the Iraqi embassy and a health certificate from an accredited health department.
iraq.dates: Under IQS/1847/1999, foods with a shelf life of three months or less need production and expiry dates printed permanently as day, month and year; stickers are not permitted.
iraq.testing: COSQC and the ministries of agriculture and health test imports at the border, and the Ministry of Health tests samples in provincial laboratories or the Central Health Laboratory in Baghdad.

syria.application: The importer applies in writing to the Ministry’s Directorate of Animal Health on its form, with a valid commercial register, a copy of an ID and a proforma invoice.
syria.disease_free: Fish and fish products must come with a health certificate stating that they come from an area or establishment free of bacterial, viral and fungal infectious fish diseases.
syria.laboratory: Fish for human consumption must come with an analysis certificate from an accredited laboratory in the country of origin showing that they are free of pathogens.
syria.labels: Fish packages must carry a clear label with the scientific and common names, the country of origin, the size category, the packing and shipping date and the producer’s name and address.
syria.shelf_life: No more than half of the fish’s shelf life may have passed when it reaches Syria.
syria.veterinary_certificate: The veterinary certificate for animal products must be issued by authorised bodies in the country of origin and authenticated by Syria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs; countries of the Greater Arab Free Trade Area are exempt from this authentication.
